title.en: Use the ideal and practical diode models

say.en: Measure a diode's resistance at two different currents and you get two different answers. A diode does not obey Ohm's law, so we need two kinds of resistance. In this lesson: Distinguish static and dynamic resistance.
State the main diode ratings.
Use the ideal and practical diode models.

body.en: *Static* (d.c.) resistance is the ratio of the d.c. voltage to the d.c. current at the operating point: $R_{dc} = V/I$. Dynamic (a.c.) resistance is the ratio of a small change in voltage to the resulting change in current: $r_d = \Delta V/\Delta I$, the reciprocal of the slope of the V–I curve. In forward bias, $r_d \approx \eta V_T/I$, only a few ohms at milliampere currents. In reverse bias both resistances are very large.

narration.en: Static resistance is V over I at the operating point. Dynamic resistance is the change in V over the change in I, and it is only a few ohms at normal forward currents.
narration.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರ ರೋಧ = ಕಾರ್ಯ ಬಿಂದುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ V/I. ಚಲನಾತ್ಮಕ ರೋಧ = ΔV/ΔI; ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಮುಮ್ಮುಖ ಪ್ರವಾಹಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಇದು ಕೆಲವೇ ಓಮ್‌ಗಳು.

say.en: Static resistance is V over I at the operating point. Dynamic resistance is the change in V over the change in I, and it is only a few ohms at normal forward currents. R dc equals V over I.
say.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರ ರೋಧ equals ಕಾರ್ಯ ಬಿಂದುವಿನಲ್ಲಿ V over I. ಚಲನಾತ್ಮಕ ರೋಧ equals delta V over delta I; ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಮುಮ್ಮುಖ ಪ್ರವಾಹಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಇದು ಕೆಲವೇ ಓಮ್‌ಗಳು.

say.en: r d equals delta V over delta I is approximately eta V T over I.
Reverse resistance: very high M ohms.
Here is the forward curve of a silicon diode. Pick an operating point Q on it.
Static resistance is V divided by I at Q: the slope of the line from the origin, turned upside down.
Dynamic resistance uses the tangent at Q: a small change in V divided by the change in I. It is much smaller than the static value.
An ideal diode is a switch: a short circuit in forward bias and an open circuit in reverse bias. A practical one adds 0.7 volt and a small resistance.
Ratings to remember: peak inverse voltage, maximum forward current and power.

body.en: A *diode*'s data sheet gives its maximum forward current I_F(max), peak inverse voltage (PIV), maximum power dissipation and reverse saturation current; exceeding them damages the diode. For circuit work we use models: the ideal diode is a switch (short circuit in forward bias, open circuit in reverse bias); the practical model adds a 0.7 V drop (Si) and, if needed, a small forward resistance. So a diode can be used as an electronic switch.

narration.en: Never exceed a diode's peak inverse voltage, maximum forward current or power rating. The ideal diode is a perfect switch; the practical model adds a 0.7 volt drop.
narration.kn: ಡಯೋಡ್‌ನ PIV, ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಮುಮ್ಮುಖ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ರೇಟಿಂಗ್ ಮೀರಬಾರದು. ಆದರ್ಶ ಡಯೋಡ್ ಒಂದು ಪರಿಪೂರ್ಣ ಸ್ವಿಚ್; ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕ ಮಾದರಿ 0.7 ವೋಲ್ಟ್ ಇಳಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: A silicon diode carries 20 mA at 0.70 V and 30 mA at 0.72 V. Find (a) its static resistance at 20 mA and (b) its dynamic resistance between the two points.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A silicon diode carries 20 mA at 0.70 V and 30 mA at 0.72 V. Find (a) its static resistance at 20 mA and (b) its dynamic resistance between the two points.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A silicon diode carries 20 milliamperes at 0.70 volts and 30 milliamperes at 0.72 volts. Find a its static resistance at 20 milliamperes and b its dynamic resistance between the two points.
R dc equals V over I equals 0.70 over 0.020 equals 35 ohms.
delta V equals 0.72 minus 0.70 equals 0.02 volts; delta I equals 30 minus 20 equals 10 milliamperes.
r d equals delta V over delta I equals 0.02 over 0.010 equals 2 ohms.
So the answer is R dc equals 35 ohms; r d equals 2 ohms.

problem.en: A 12 V battery drives a silicon diode in series with a 1 kΩ resistor (forward bias). Find the current using (a) the ideal model and (b) the practical model.

steps.en: Ideal: the diode is a short, so I = 12/1000 = 12 mA.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 12 V battery drives a silicon diode in series with a 1 kΩ resistor (forward bias). Find the current using (a) the ideal model and (b) the practical model.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 12 volts battery drives a silicon diode in series with a 1 k ohms resistor forward bias. Find the current using a the ideal model and b the practical model.
Ideal: the diode is a short, so I equals 12 over 1000 equals 12 milliamperes.
Practical: subtract 0.7 volts: I equals 12 minus 0.7/1000 equals 11.3 milliamperes.
So the answer is 12 milliamperes ideal; 11.3 milliamperes practical.
